description:
FILED s473f (Opus, 2026-09-09).  PRE-EXISTING.

    open(*Foo::STDOUT, '>', $F) or die;
    print "to-real-stdout\n";
    print {*Foo::STDOUT} "to-foo\n";

    perl : the file holds "to-foo\n"; stdout holds "to-real-stdout\n"
    PCL  : the file is EMPTY and BOTH lines went to stdout

%p-resolve-fh's typeglob arm looks the glob's NAME up with
`(find-symbol NAME :pcl)` and only falls back to a scan of *p-filehandles*.
For `*Foo::STDOUT` that finds pcl::stdout -- the STANDARD handle -- so a glob
in another package resolves to the wrong stream.  %p-install-fh's twin arm
interns in `(p-typeglob-package glob)`, but `intern` finds an INHERITED symbol
too (every user package :uses :pcl), so the two sides can agree on the wrong
symbol as easily as on the right one.

s473f's #1220 fix made %p-std-slot stop treating `*Foo::STDOUT` as STDOUT (that
half is fixed and guarded, row 09 of the std-handle cases); the READ side is
this task.  The fix is presumably "ask the glob's OWN package first, with a
symbol that is not merely inherited", which needs a probe of what PCL's package
graph makes reachable.  Probe scratch/s473f/p4b-stdpkg.pl row 01.


=== PARTLY FIXED (s532c, Opus agent, 2026-11-06): the read half's NAME SCAN ===
A second, silent symptom of the same typeglob arm: `\*DATA` in main resolved by NAME across every package's handles, so a program that loads a module with an `__END__` section (PCL installs a DATA handle per package) read whichever DATA the hash met first -- Template-Toolkit t/filter.t's `test_expect(\*DATA, ...)` read a module's one-newline section and planned 4 tests where perl plans 164.  FIX: %p-resolve-fh's typeglob arm asks the glob's OWN package first (%p-typeglob-own-symbol: a symbol PRESENT in the glob's package, never one inherited from :pcl; nothing interned) before the :pcl symbol and the name scan.  TT filter.t: 164/0 (= perl).  Guard `Pl/t/glob-defined-01.t` row 3.
STILL OPEN (measured s532c, base ce665621 and tree alike): this task's own reproducer.  `open(*Foo::STDOUT, '>', $F)` CLOSES THE REAL STDOUT -- every later print to STDOUT is lost and the file stays empty (scratch/s532c/p/1423-b.pl: perl prints "00 start / 01 to-real-stdout / 02 end" and the file holds "to-foo"; PCL prints "00 start" and nothing else, rc 0).  %p-install-fh's %p-close-previous-stream resolves the glob before the open registers it: the own-package symbol Foo::stdout does not exist yet, so the typeglob arm falls through to (find-symbol "stdout" :pcl) = the standard handle and closes it.  The fix shape: the :pcl fallback must not answer a glob QUALIFIED in a non-main package for a forced-main name (perl's *Foo::STDOUT is not STDOUT) -- probe the unqualified `*STDOUT` in package Foo (perl: main's) on the way.  Also left: the name scan's last resort still answers another package's same-named handle where perl has none (`open XX ...` in main, `\*XX` in package Q reads main's; perl reads nothing).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a typeglob's PACKAGE is dropped when it is resolved as a filehandle -- `*Foo::STDOUT` reaches the standard handle
